original_test_intent: Prove that the exact GB-NV-PVP PCIe Gen5 channel can move from Gen1 to Gen5 at full required width five hundred times with valid training/equalization and no new endpoint, link, or system errors.
original_method: First establish that every path element supports the requested Gen5 width and that Speed Change 15 is valid; capture baseline; execute five hundred serial transactions that record Gen1 entry, Gen5 request, intermediate LTSSM/equalization, final gen/width, errors, and platform health; inhibit subsequent changes on the first unsupported, incomplete, or failed result and use an approved recovery route.
manual_activity: The platform and signal-integrity owners approve Gen5 capability and the Speed Change 15 recipe; lab personnel isolate the SUT and own out-of-band recovery from high-generation link instability.
required_inputs: Documented Gen5 capability for root port, retimer/switch, board/backplane/cabling, endpoint/GPU, firmware, and required lanes
Pinned Gen5 LTSSM/NVQual Speed Change 15 package/configuration
Gen1 entry, Gen5 request, equalization/LTSSM trajectory, target width, and settle timeout
Five-hundred-count, transient, error-delta, artifact-integrity, abort, final-state, and recovery rules
safety_requirements: Do not begin repetitive stress until end-to-end Gen5 capability is confirmed
Use a dedicated SUT with stable power/cooling and out-of-band console
Hard-stop on unsupported target, equalization/retrain failure, reduced width, new AER, endpoint/GPU/host loss, reset, thermal/power anomaly, or collection gap
Never downgrade acceptance, continue, or retry automatically
agent_execution_scope: Verify signed-off Gen5 capability, topology, tool, and criteria
Execute only the approved Speed Change 15 operation
Persist each complete transaction and inhibit the next on anomaly
Correlate physical-path link behavior with error and platform health
Do not assume capability from device naming, accept Gen4/reduced width, alter other links, retry, or issue a formal verdict
engineer_actions: Approve end-to-end Gen5 channel and target width
Own lab risk, first-fault disposition, and recovery
Review all 500 transactions and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It names the expected tool family but cannot establish Gen5 capability or Speed Change 15 semantics, and a final link/error sweep is inadequate for the five-hundred-transaction criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the owner-pinned Gen5 Speed Change 15 transaction only after capability sign-off, recording initial, training/equalization, final width/speed, and error/health evidence atomically.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: LTSSM, 500 Gen1-to-Gen5 transitions, expected width/speed, no errors, no bundle, and 30/180-minute allocation remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate the support gate from the stress run, then maintain a fail-closed ledger for every high-generation transition and its channel/equalization outcome.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the essential Gen5 feasibility proof, physical-channel scope, transaction semantics, and recovery controls absent from the short row.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Gen4 success, reduced width, or one final Gen5 observation cannot satisfy repeated full-width Gen5 transition coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Gen5 channel margin is highly topology- and implementation-dependent; repeated equalization can trigger downtraining, AER, endpoint loss, GPU/host reset, or extended lab outage.

project_override_considerations: If the approved GB-NV-PVP topology does not support Gen5 at the required width, execution is BLOCKED and the review must not reinterpret the case as Gen4. Do not combine evidence with lower-generation Speed Change rows.

Raw monotonic 1-500 transaction ledger with Gen1, request, equalization/LTSSM, settled Gen5/full-width, timestamps, and results
First-fault recovery or clean final state plus engineer verdict

review_improvement: Adds an explicit feasibility gate and fail-closed Gen5 evidence model, preventing unsupported, downgraded, or final-snapshot results from being counted as the requested coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The label Gen5 is a capability claim about the entire channel, not only the endpoint. A single Gen4-limited retimer, board segment, root port, or firmware setting makes the requested target impossible even if the qualification binary accepts a Gen5 option. Capability must therefore be verified before a 500-cycle stress loop is authorized. At Gen5, equalization behavior and corrected-error deltas are integral to margin assessment; the final negotiated field alone can hide repeated recovery or width loss. A fail-closed transaction ledger prevents such marginal behavior from being overwritten by subsequent transitions.
